text: I keep telling people: the real moat in AI isn't the model, it's the feedback loop between model, data, and deployment. Whoever closes that loop fastest wins. 训练、数据、部署的闭环速度，才是真正的护城河。

We're rolling out a new reasoning model with dramatically improved multi-step planning. It can now decompose a complex engineering task into verifiable subtasks, execute them, and self-correct mid-flight. Available to all Plus users today.
The cost of intelligence is falling faster than the cost of compute did in the 90s. In a few years, 'can we afford to think about this problem' will sound as weird as 'can we afford to google it'.

smolagents v2 is out 🎉 Our minimal agentic framework now supports multi-agent delegation, sandboxed tool execution, and a 40% faster reasoning loop. 300 lines of core code. Try it: github.com/huggingface/smolagents

Autoregressive LLMs are dead ends for reasoning. They can't plan. JEPA-style architectures that learn world models from raw sensory data are the path to machines that actually understand cause and effect. We've made progress; more soon.

Small language models (5-20B) fine-tuned on domain data are beating giant general models at enterprise tasks at 1/20th the inference cost. The 'bigger is always better' era is officially over for most business use cases.

AlphaProof + AlphaGeometry achieve silver-medal level on IMO geometry problems. We're sharing the approach: a neuro-symbolic loop where a learned model proposes, a symbolic engine verifies. Paper + code released today.

Our new prompt-caching feature cuts long-context API costs by up to 90%. If you're building agents that loop over the same system prompt, this is the single biggest bill reduction we've shipped this year.

Just watched a demo where an agent debugged a broken codebase, wrote the fix, shipped it, and wrote the postmortem. We are rapidly approaching the point where the bottleneck in software is deciding WHAT to build, not building it.

New fine-tuning API: upload 100 examples, get a model that follows your style guide, tone, and formatting rules. We've seen 3x better instruction adherence vs prompt-engineering alone on internal evals.

10,000 people on the waitlist for our new device. The next platform shift isn't a website, it's hardware that's always with you and always listening to context. AI-native devices will make phones feel like desktop PCs.

We just benchmarked 40 open LLMs for tool calling. Surprise: a 7B model fine-tuned on function-calling data outperforms most 70B+ models. Quality of tool-use training data >> raw parameter count. Full report on the blog.

Today's AI has the intelligence of a smart parrot. It predicts words, not consequences. Until models act in the world and suffer the consequences of their errors, they will never be truly intelligent. Embodiment is not optional.

AI agents will create more jobs than they displace — but the jobs will look different. The winning skill set for 2026: knowing how to decompose a business process into steps an agent can automate. Learn to delegate to machines.

Veo 3.5 can now generate 8-minute cinematic videos with consistent characters and controllable camera moves from a single image + prompt. Filmmakers: your pre-production just got 10x cheaper. Sign up for the API waitlist.

Interpretability update: we can now trace which internal features activate when Claude reasons about 'deception'. Circuits work is moving from the lab to safety evals — we're open-sourcing the tooling to inspect your own models.

A practical tip for anyone building RAG: chunking by semantic paragraphs beats fixed token windows by ~15% on retrieval quality. And re-ranking is the single most underrated step in the pipeline. Ship a reranker before you ship a fancier embedder.

Vision-to-action agents are here: describe a UI bug in natural language with a screenshot, and our agent will reproduce, diagnose, and file a fix PR. We estimate 40% of QA tickets can be fully automated this way.

We will soon ship 'memory that persists across projects'. Your AI should remember your codebase style, your writing voice, and your past decisions — without you re-explaining them every session. This is table stakes for real assistants.
Introducing gradio-realtime: build voice & video agents with live streaming UI in 20 lines of Python. WebRTC under the hood, zero backend config. Star the repo and give it a spin this weekend.

Reading today's arXiv: 30+ papers on 'agent frameworks'. None of them measure anything. Please, run the benchmarks. Compare against a baseline. Publish your eval harness. The field is drowning in demos and starving for measurement.

Free lesson drop: how to build a RAG system that actually answers questions instead of hallucinating. 45 minutes, notebook included, covers hybrid search + reranking + citation grounding. Link in thread. Happy learning!

Gemma 3.2 open model family: 1B to 27B, multimodal, 128K context, and it runs on a single consumer GPU. We believe frontier open models and frontier closed models will converge on capability within 18 months. Here's the eval table.

Claude's new 'research mode' reads 200 sources, cross-checks claims, and returns a cited brief instead of a confident guess. Early enterprise feedback: 6 hours of analyst work compressed into 12 minutes. Feedback loop begins now.

nanoGPT rewrite is done. 700 lines of PyTorch, zero dependencies beyond torch, trains a real GPT-2-scale model on a single 8xH100 node in under a day. The best way to actually understand transformers is still to train one yourself.

Safety report released: our evals found the new model refuses 22% fewer legitimate requests while maintaining safety guardrails on 99.2% of red-team probes. Transparency on both axes — helpfulness and harm — is how we build trust.

Observation: the teams winning with AI are not the ones with the most GPUs. They are the ones with the best evaluation loops. A 10-person team measuring weekly beats a 100-person team shipping vibes. Eval culture is the new engineering culture.

Our model hub crossed 2 million public models this week. The new 'model health' score shows you freshness, license compliance, and security scan status at a glance. Choosing an open model just got a lot safer.

The next 5 years belong to world models. Prediction: within 3 years, the dominant architecture for video generation will be a learned latent world model, not a next-token predictor. Bookmark this tweet.

Why every company should have an 'AI kitchen' — a small team with permission to prototype aggressively, no ROI pressure, with a mandate to ship one working demo every two weeks. The best AI orgs I consult for all have one.

AlphaFold 4 preview: prediction time down from minutes to seconds, structure + function + interactions in a single pass, and it's 8x more accurate on protein complexes. Drug discovery timelines are about to shrink again.

Cost transparency month: we're publishing per-task token economics for 12 common agent workloads. Spoiler: agents that reuse context pay 70% less. Prompt caching isn't a feature, it's a business model.

Hot take: 'prompt engineering' is a temporary skill, but 'data engineering' is permanent. Models get smarter every quarter; your dataset stays yours. Build the pipeline that turns your company's history into tokens. That's the real moat.

ChatGPT memory is now cross-modal: it can remember what you look like in video calls, how you structure documents, and which design direction you prefer — then apply all of it without being asked. Opt-in, on-device first, fully exportable.

We're hiring for 'AI product people' — engineers who think in terms of capabilities, not features. If you can spec an agent workflow the way you'd spec an API, you will out-earn 90% of your peers in the next five years. The shift is that big.

Open-source agent leaderboard v3 is live: 50 frameworks, 3,000 tasks, human-verified. Key finding: tool-calling reliability matters 3x more than reasoning score for real tasks. Optimize the boring part. Report: hf.co/papers/agents-v3

Project Mariner update: our browser agent can now complete multi-step purchases with price comparisons, coupon hunting, and return-policy checks. Safety rails included. E-commerce agents are closer than the skeptics think.

Batch reasoning is the underrated trick: ask the model to produce 10 candidate solutions in one call, then have it (or a judge model) pick the best. Cost +30%, quality + lots. Cheaper than self-consistency loops and easier to ship.

My definition of AGI: a system that can learn any task a human can, with comparable data efficiency, and transfer learning across tasks. By that standard, today's best models are at the level of a well-trained 5-year-old — in narrow domains. Long way to go.

Claude Code is now 25% faster and uses 30% fewer tokens on long sessions thanks to context distillation. Also: you can now spawn 3 parallel subagents from one session. Your repo's next feature can write itself while you review.
